decision: Benchmark the real submitted mission DAG with deterministic synthetic durations and enforce a latency/concurrency readiness gate before real Qubes workers.
winner: critical-path DAG benchmark over OrchestratedMissionRuntime output

criteria.correctness: Uses the actual durable mission graph, validates missing dependencies/cycles, and derives timing from dependency completion rather than a hand-written phase formula.
criteria.robustness: Deterministic inputs make regressions reproducible and independent of host timing noise.
criteria.latency: Measures serial baseline, fan-out critical path, latency saved, and speedup directly.
criteria.resourceUse: Measures peak concurrent missions while verifying total synthetic work does not increase.
criteria.regressionRisk: Read-only benchmark logic; no changes to queue persistence, claims, worker transport, or orchestration semantics.
criteria.qa: Covers a real runtime-generated two-specialist DAG, readiness pass/fail behavior, missing dependency rejection, cycle rejection, and incomplete fixture rejection.

alternatives.approach: wall-clock sleeps with live worker loops
alternatives.reason: Closer to runtime latency but noisy in CI, slower, and vulnerable to host scheduling variance. Keep for later process/Qubes acceptance testing.
Fast but can pass even if the real mission dependency graph regresses.
Highest observability but adds infrastructure and operational surface before real-worker readiness.

lessons: Benchmark the graph that workers actually consume, not a parallel model of intended behavior.
Separate deterministic structural performance gates from noisy end-to-end wall-clock acceptance tests.
Latency wins are not sufficient alone; cap peak concurrency so fan-out cannot hide excessive resource pressure.
safety: Synthetic timing only. No real financial transactions, payment data, external exploitation, or weakened controls.
